signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Cross-Asset Stress
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5630, sitting well below its SMA20/50/200 technical cluster at 0.8254/0.8228/0.8000 on USD/CHF and 0.6997/0.7053/0.7060 on AUD/USD. The G10 currency scorecard flags a major bilateral divergence with CHF outperforming G10 peers at +1.240% (n=6) while AUD lags at -2.182% (n=4), generating a 3.422% leader-to-laggard spread. Safe-haven demand for CHF is accelerating amid global risk-off sentiment driven by a 5.96% drop in the Nikkei 225, pushing VIX to 26.8 (elevated volatility). An extreme +485bp rate differential (RBA at 4.85% vs SNB at 0.00%) fails to protect the Aussie as high-beta carry trades unwind in an elevated volatility regime. BEER fair value model shows AUD/CHF stretched at z=-2.80σ cheap (spot 0.5640 vs fair value 0.5748), but strong structural momentum prevents immediate mean reversion. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF; flight-to-quality overrides extreme carry advantage while equity stress persists. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 13:30 UTC. Risk: VIX retracts below 20 and equity markets stabilize, allowing carry differentials to reassert.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Equity Risk-Off
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.36, holding below its SMA20 at 157.95 and SMA200 at 158.63 while anchoring inside a tight 20-session range. A 271bp OIS carry differential (SOFR 3.94% vs TONA 1.23%) provides structural baseline support for USD, though broad equity liquidations keep upside momentum in check. Options markets exhibit heavy defensive positioning, with the 1M 25-delta Risk Reversal printing a strong put skew of -1.80, signalling institutional demand for downside JPY protection despite flat COT positioning (pctl 94%, WoW +6,374). Cross-asset correlation between USD/JPY and VIX sits at +0.074 vs the 252-day norm of +0.300 (z=-1.98σ), demonstrating that standard JPY safe-haven appreciation remains muted during equity drawdowns. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; strong carry support competes directly with downside options hedging and broad equity liquidation. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls and Unemployment Rate at 13:30 UTC. Risk: VIX spikes above 30, driving a broader carry unwind that breaks USD/JPY below SMA50 support at 157.33.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT-OIS Divergence + Volatility Complacency
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6878, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6997/0.7053/0.7060, confirming an active technical downtrend. CFTC leveraged funds hold a net long position of +43,927 contracts, whereas the 1-week spot price is down -2.13%, reflecting institutional positioning that is stubbornly fighting the prevailing trend. FX options reflect extreme pricing complacency with 1M ATM IV at 6.2% against HV30 at 7.9%, generating a negative Vol Risk Premium of -1.8% alongside a -0.87 25d Risk Reversal put skew. RBA policy rate sits at 4.85% vs Fed at 4.00% (-91bp OIS spread favoring AUD), but rate differentials are failing to cushion spot against global commodity and Asian equity weakness. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD; negative vol risk premium and stagnant spec long positioning leave the pair vulnerable to further downside liquidation. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Strong US labor market deterioration weakens the USD and triggers a squeeze back toward the 0.6997 SMA20 level.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Negativity + Retail Sentiment Extreme
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5546, holding well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5642/0.5703/0.5825 amidst a range-bound technical backdrop. New Zealand's Economic Surprise Index sits at a severe -25.1 rating, highlighting persistent macroeconomic data misses against expectations. Retail sentiment data retail positioning shows an extreme 91% long vs 9% short bias, creating a stark contrarian signal as retail traders attempt to bottom-fish a falling spot rate. COT leveraged funds remain net short -22,722 contracts (pctl 25%), demonstrating that institutional capital is aligned with the macroeconomic degradation while retail is trapped on the wrong side. Fed at 4.00% vs RBNZ at 2.75% provides a +125bp OIS carry advantage to the USD (SOFR 3.94% vs OCR 2.75%), compounding the fundamental pressure on the Kiwi. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; institutional shorts and weak data beats outweigh retail bottom-fishing efforts. Catalyst: US Michigan Consumer Sentiment at 15:00 UTC. Risk: US data misses sharply, easing USD rate dominance and forcing a short-squeeze above 0.5642 SMA20.
